summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or output format consistently, or encode domain-specific patterns that cannot be captured in a prompt or context window; it excels at instruction adherence, tone, structured outputs, and latency/cost reduction via smaller specialized models. RAG is the better choice when you need the model to access frequently-changing or factual knowledge, while prompt engineering should always be exhausted first for its zero training cost and fast iteration. In practice, teams often combine a lightly fine-tuned base model with RAG for knowledge grounding.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output format, tone, or domain-specific behavior that prompting alone cannot reliably enforce across thousands of examples.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when the required knowledge changes frequently or must be factually grounded and citable, since fine-tuning bakes information in statically.
Fine-tune to reduce inference cost and latency by distilling capabilities into a smaller model rather than relying on large-prompt calls to a frontier model.
Only fine-tune after prompt engineering and RAG have been exhausted, and when you have a few hundred to thousands of high-quality labeled examples available.

tools.name: Together AI
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-token and per-GPU-hour; fine-tuning priced per trained token with discounted serverless inference (e.g. ~$176/day at 50M daily output tokens example)

tools.name: Vertex AI
